19	# 论文写作风格规范
20	
21	> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。
22	
23	---
24	
25	## 一、总体写作哲学
26	
27	### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌
28	
29	- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
30	- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
31	- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
32	- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing
33	
34	### 1.2 主线统一性
35	
36	- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
37	- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
38	- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
39	- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线
40	
41	### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义
42	
43	- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
44	- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
45	- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
46	- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug
47	
48	### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文
49	
50	- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
51	- 重点学：
52	  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
53	  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
54	  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
55	  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
56	- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
57	- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文
58	
59	---
60	
61	## 二、Abstract 写作规范
62	
63	### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）
64	
65	Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
66	1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
67	2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
68	3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
69	4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献
70	
71	### 2.2 禁忌
72	
73	- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
74	- **

1	Frozen Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can be improved at inference time without modifying weights, but existing approaches either apply correction unconditionally or require prohibitive compute.
2	We propose ACR-VLA, a lightweight adaptive correction pipeline for frozen flow-matching VLAs. At each control step, the pipeline draws $K{=}2$ action samples in a single batched forward pass and uses their pairwise $L_2$ distance ($\rho{=}0.9979$ vs.\ $K{=}10$ sample variance) as a per-step uncertainty gate. Low-uncertainty steps output the argmin-to-centroid sample directly; high-uncertainty steps apply bounded residual correction via a Correction Residual Module (CRM). The pipeline uses at most two VLA forward passes---performance gains come from learned correction, not additional sampling.
3	We validate ACR-VLA across three flow-matching VLAs (SmolVLA 0.4B, $\pi_{0.5}$ 3.6B, OpenVLA-OFT 7B) on four LIBERO benchmark suites. On SmolVLA, ACR-VLA achieves $18.3$\% on LIBERO-Object ($+$7.3\,pp vs.\ VLA-only) and $35.0$\% on LIBERO-Spatial ($+$5.6\,pp), matching fixed-$K{=}10$ unconditional correction with 80\% fewer forward passes. Systematic analysis reveals that learned correction is the active mechanism (55--78\% of the gain), while multi-sampling provides enabling centering---random selection alone fails to improve over VLA-only on either benchmark.

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:intro}

\looseness=-1 Deploying a pretrained Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model on a new task usually requires fine-tuning on task demonstrations, yet collecting that data is expensive and the resulting checkpoint may not transfer further. A more attractive route keeps the VLA frozen and improves action quality at inference time. Flow-matching VLAs~\cite{black2024pi0,shukor2025smolvla,lipman2023flow} fit this setting because each forward pass produces a stochastic action sample, so drawing multiple samples opens a path to selection and correction without retraining~\cite{snell2024scaling}. The naive instantiation draws $K{=}10$ samples per control step and either averages them or applies an unconditional correction, but most control steps are easy and the extra forward passes are wasted compute. The question we ask is whether the same gain is reachable with adaptive, per-step allocation.

\looseness=-1 Recent work touches parts of this question without answering it. A2C2~\cite{a2c2_2025} learns a correction head on action chunks but applies it unconditionally and inherits the temporal staleness of fixed chunks. ReconVLA~\cite{chen2026reconvla} quantifies uncertainty over frozen VLAs but does not learn a corrective residual. SC-VLA~\cite{liu2026scvla} uses reinforcement learning on the base policy and therefore does not stay weight-frozen. VLA-Pilot~\cite{li2025vlapilot} performs evolutionary search at $2.41$\,s per control step, which rules out closed-loop deployment. None of these address the core efficiency question: can a frozen VLA decide \emph{per step} whether it needs additional sampling and correction at all?

\looseness=-1 We propose \textbf{ACR-VLA}, an adaptive inference-time pipeline for frozen flow-matching VLAs. ACR-VLA draws only $K{=}2$ samples in a single batched forward pass and uses their pairwise $L_2$ distance as a per-step uncertainty estimate. This minimal probe is well-calibrated: Spearman $\rho{=}0.9979$ against the $K{=}10$ sample variance computed offline, whereas three alternatives (flow-matching velocity divergence, CRM correction magnitude at $K{=}1$ and at $K{=}2$) all yield $\rho \leq 0.15$. When the probe falls below threshold, the pipeline outputs the argmin-to-centroid sample directly; when it exceeds threshold, a lightweight Correction Residual Module (CRM, ${\sim}$327K parameters, $<\!1\%$ of the SmolVLA backbone) applies a bounded residual to the same sample. The pipeline uses at most two VLA forward passes per step, and batched $K{=}2$ inference matches single-sample latency (${\sim}253$\,ms).

\looseness=-1 On SmolVLA, ACR-VLA reaches $18.3 \pm 2.1$\% on LIBERO-Object ($+$7.3\,pp over the $11.0 \pm 1.3$\% VLA-only baseline, 8 seeds) and $35.0 \pm 1.0$\% on LIBERO-Spatial ($+$5.6\,pp over $29.4 \pm 1.5$\%, 5 seeds). The adaptive pipeline reaches the same task success as the fixed-$K{=}10$ unconditional pipeline while issuing 80\% fewer VLA forward passes. We then apply the identical recipe, with only the per-task CRM retrained, to two larger flow-matching VLAs ($\pi_{0.5}$~\cite{black2024pi0} at $3.6$B and OpenVLA-OFT~\cite{kim2024openvla} at $7$B) across all four LIBERO suites~\cite{liu2023libero} (Object, Spatial, Goal, Long). The pipeline is VLA-agnostic by design: the $K{=}2$ probe, argmin selection, and bounded CRM correction do not depend on backbone scale or task family.

\looseness=-1 An ablation isolates where the gain comes from. Learned correction contributes $55$\% of the gain at $K{=}5$ and $78$\% at $K{=}10$, while random sample selection on its own fails to improve over the VLA-only baseline on either benchmark. Multi-sampling supplies a centered starting point and the uncertainty gate, but the active mechanism is the residual. This finding shaped the adaptive design: scaling samples beyond $K{=}2$ buys little once the correction is in place, so the budget is better spent on the residual than on extra sampling.

Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,nosep]
  \item \textbf{ACR-VLA pipeline} (Section~\ref{sec:method}): an adaptive $K{=}2$ uncertainty-gated CRM correction pipeline for frozen flow-matching VLAs. ACR-VLA reaches $18.3$\% on LIBERO-Object and $35.0$\% on LIBERO-Spatial ($+$7.3 / $+$5.6\,pp over VLA-only) and matches the $K{=}10$ unconditional pipeline with 80\% fewer forward passes.
  \item \textbf{Cross-VLA validation} (Section~\ref{sec:main_results}): the same recipe is evaluated on three flow-matching VLAs spanning $0.4$B to $7$B parameters and on all four LIBERO suites, providing evidence that the design is VLA-agnostic.
  \item \textbf{Component analysis} (Section~\ref{sec:main_results}): learned correction is the active mechanism (55--78\% of the gain), multi-sampling provides centering, and random selection alone fails to improve. This analysis motivated the adaptive gate.
  \item \textbf{Applicability boundaries} (Section~\ref{sec:failure_modes}): stochastic VLA diversity is a prerequisite (tokenized VLAs are near-deterministic and lie outside scope), and the CRM requires task-specific calibration rather than a single global checkpoint.
\end{enumerate}

ACR-VLA: Adaptive Conformal Refinement
for Frozen Flow-Matching VLAs
Anonymous Author(s)
Affiliation

Abstract: Frozen Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can be improved at inference time without modifying weights, but existing approaches either apply correction unconditionally or require prohibitive compute. We propose ACR-VLA, a
lightweight adaptive correction pipeline for frozen flow-matching VLAs. At each
control step, the pipeline draws K=2 action samples in a single batched forward
pass and uses their pairwise L2 distance (ρ=0.9979 vs. K=10 sample variance) as
a per-step uncertainty gate. Low-uncertainty steps output the argmin-to-centroid
sample directly; high-uncertainty steps apply bounded residual correction via a
Correction Residual Module (CRM). The pipeline uses at most two VLA forward passes—performance gains come from learned correction, not additional
sampling. We validate ACR-VLA across three flow-matching VLAs (SmolVLA
0.4B, π0.5 3.6B, OpenVLA-OFT 7B) on four LIBERO benchmark suites. On
SmolVLA, ACR-VLA achieves 18.3% on LIBERO-Object (+7.3 pp vs. VLAonly) and 35.0% on LIBERO-Spatial (+5.6 pp), matching fixed-K=10 unconditional correction with 80% fewer forward passes. Systematic analysis reveals that
learned correction is the active mechanism (55–78% of the gain), while multisampling provides enabling centering—random selection alone fails to improve
over VLA-only on either benchmark.
